newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says value of non-oil exports up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says value of non-oil exports up in 1996.

text.p: The value of Saudi Arabia's non-oil exports are projected to rise by around 26 percent this year, Commerce Minister Osama bin Jaafar bin Ibrahim Faqih was on Monday quoted as saying.
He said Saudi non-oil exports for 1996 are projected to reach 30 billion riyals ($8 billion) compared to 23.7 billion riyals in 1995, Saudi newspapers reported.

Faqih said Saudi Arabia -- the world's largest oil producer and exporter -- was taking steps to boost its non-oil exports, including strengthening trade missions abroad and providing "suitable credit guarantee and protection for the exports."
Saudi Arabia relies on its export of some six million barrels per day of crude oil for 75 percent of its revenue, but has in recent years been trying to diversify its economy.
The kingdom expects in its 1995-2000 development plan its non-oil sector to grow by an average 3.9 percent a year.
